title: Chopin, Waltz Op. 64 No. 2, in four recordings
work: Waltz in C♯ minor, Op. 64 No. 2
question: How do these four pianists make the circling tune answer the slower melodies?
intro: Paderewski, Pachmann, Rummel and Gurevich all begin with the same opening, a melody held back over a bass that keeps moving. Chopin sets quick quavers running between that C♯-minor melody and a second one in D♭ major. The circling refrain returns repeatedly and closes the piece.

recordings.label: Ignacy Jan Paderewski, 1917
recordings.note: Paderewski’s Victor recordings preserve his habit of spreading chords and letting the melody arrive separately from the bass.

recordings.label: Vladimir de Pachmann, 1925
recordings.note: Pachmann plays his own Baldwin at Hayes, with his own variant in bars 82–83.

recordings.label: Walter Morse Rummel, 1943
recordings.note: Rummel had introduced Debussy’s complete second book of Préludes in London in 1913.

recordings.label: Olga Gurevich, c. 2014
recordings.note: Gurevich grew up studying piano in Baku. Her teachers’ ideal of a singing tone is central to her own teaching.

passages.label: Opening waltz
passages.note: Held notes cross the bar line, then a quick figure follows. The bass keeps its pattern of one note and two chords.

passages.label: Second phrase of the opening melody
passages.note: The opening melody completes another phrase, with short flourishes placed between longer notes. The waltz accompaniment continues.

passages.label: Più mosso in quavers
passages.note: The right hand plays chains of quavers, marked più mosso (more movement). The left hand continues beneath it.

passages.label: Falling and rising quaver figure
passages.note: The quick tune falls, rises and falls again, its turns fitted across the left hand’s three-beat pattern.

passages.label: Più lento in D♭ major
passages.note: The piano moves to D♭ major and a broader melody. The marking Più lento calls for a slower tempo.

passages.label: Return of the opening melody
passages.note: The opening C♯-minor melody returns with its held notes and short answering flourishes, and the quick refrain closes the piece.
